**Meeting.** Troy School District Board of Education, Organizational Meeting and Regular Meeting, Tuesday, January 17, 2012, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098 (administration at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000).

**Organizational business.** Superintendent Barbara A. Fowler's agenda memo sets the procedure: the prior year's president acts as chairperson, Judy Holmes is appointed temporary secretary, and four votes are required to elect each officer. Officers serve until December 31, 2012. Item 6.B appoints Mark S. Rajter, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, as Treasurer for January through December 2012, a nonvoting officer under Board Policy. Item 6.C adopts the Fund Depositories and Investment Resolution naming Bank of America, Bank of New York, JP Morgan Chase Bank, Citizen's Bank, Comerica Bank, Fifth Third Bank, MILAF (Michigan Liquid Asset Fund Plus, managed by PFM Asset Management, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank), PFM Securities, Inc., and PNC Bank; investments follow Board Policy D-1103 and subsection (1)(h) of Section 380.1223 of the Revised School Code. Health-claim checks over $10,000 require the added handwritten signature of Jasen Witt or Monica Papasian. The Superintendent continues as Deputy Secretary, Judy Holmes posts notices, and a 2012 calendar of regular meetings and workshops is adopted.

**Recognitions.** 104 senior scholar athletes at a 3.5 cumulative grade point average; nine all-state athletes; and the 2011 Siemens Competition team of seniors Edgar Wang and Justin Yuan and junior Wayne Shu, who took second place in a field of 20 national finalists at George Washington University and share $50,000 in scholarships. Art teacher Heather Kelly created seven canvas pieces for Board recognition.

**December YTD FY2012 budget reports.** General Fund (101, 120, 122, 140) approved revenue $127,175,517 with $45,378,538 actual, 64.32% uncollected; approved expenditures $128,282,487 with $48,553,956 actual and $61,832,116 encumbered, 13.95% available. Excess revenue over (under) expenditures (1,106,970); fund balance July 1, 2011 of 18,803,870 and June 30, 2012 of 17,696,900. Debt Service Funds show property taxes of 19,402,035 budgeted against 8,584,779 actual, redemption of principal 12,460,000 with none paid, and interest on debt 5,790,650 with 2,895,325 paid. Capital Projects Fund 404 shows capital outlay actual of 1,675,874 against a 1,102,084 budget.

**Action and report items.** Appointment of Jasen Witt as chief spokesperson with Mark Rajter and Sara Konieczka for TESPA/MEA/NEA negotiations (contract expires June 30, 2012); probationary contracts for intervention specialists Molly Brehm (Troy Union Elementary) and Erin Hill (Baker Middle School); reports on the Oakland Community Accelerated Learning Program at Oakland Community College and the T.R.O.Y. elementary fitness program; four Schools of Choice resolutions under Sections 105 and 105c for 2012-2013 (100 kindergarten and 30 first grade nonresident students; 25 nonresident sixth through eighth graders at Baker); the second of four Superintendent goal updates; and a closed session on negotiations and attorney-client privilege.

Troy School District Board of Education packet for the Organizational Meeting and Regular Meeting of Tuesday, January 17, 2012, at 7:00 PM in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; district administration is at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Cablecast footers in the same packet print conflicting channels for TS-TV (Channel 19 and Channel 58 on Comcast, Channel 15 on WOW), Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. except July and August.

**Organizational meeting.** Superintendent Barbara A. Fowler's agenda memo provides that the previous year's president conducts the election, that Judy Holmes be appointed temporary secretary, and that four votes are required to elect. President, vice president and secretary serve until December 31, 2012, with roll-call orders rotating among Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Schmidt and Underwood. Item 6.B appoints Mark S. Rajter, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, as Treasurer of the Troy Board of Education for January through December 2012, a nonvoting officer appointed annually under Board Policy. Item 6.C adopts the Fund Depositories and Investment Resolution, certified this 17th day of January 2012 in Oakland County, Michigan. Depositories: Bank of America, Bank of New York, JP Morgan Chase Bank, Citizen's Bank, Comerica Bank, Fifth Third Bank, MILAF (Michigan Liquid Asset Fund Plus, managed by PFM Asset Management, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank), PFM Securities, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank, and PNC Bank. Checks carry Rajter's facsimile signature, with the handwritten signature of Rajter or Superintendent Fowler in emergencies on the General Fund and Payroll accounts at Bank of America; PNC accounts paying Troy Career Center expenses are signed by the Career Center Manager, Assistant Manager or Program Coordinators; health-claim checks over $10,000 require the added handwritten signature of Jasen Witt, Assistant Superintendent for Human Resources, or Finance Director Monica Papasian; Comerica flexible spending claims are paid by ACH debit to Next Generation Enrollment, Inc. Investment authority runs through Board Policy D-1103 and subsection (1)(h) of Section 380.1223 of the Revised School Code, with authorized institutions including Ambassador Capital Management, Charter One Bank, Flagstar Bancorp, Morgan Stanley Smith Barney and The Private Bank. The Superintendent continues as Deputy Secretary and Judy Holmes posts notices. The adopted 2012 calendar sets regular meetings on February 7, March 6, April 17, May 1, June 5 (Annual Recognition Meeting at Athens High School), June 19, July 10, August 14, September 4, October 2, November 6 and December 4, 2012, and January 15, 2013, with workshops including the January 27 Board Winter Retreat and a March 20 session at GROW.

**Recognitions.** 104 senior scholar athletes receive certificates for maintaining a 3.5 cumulative grade point average while participating in an athletic program (the agenda labels the item Fall while the roster is headed winter and spring). Nine all-state athletes are recognized with biographies read by Mr. Jolly: Zachary Doepke, Kelly Feng, Matthew Kuntzman, Jason Leslie, Kento Mizusaki, Sanath Shettigar, Matthew Smolinski, William Yau and Richard Zang. Seniors Edgar Wang and Justin Yuan and junior Wayne Shu, the only Michigan students in a field of 20 national finalists, share $50,000 after placing second in the 2011 Siemens Competition, whose finals were at George Washington University. Art teacher Heather Kelly, honored at ArtPrize, created seven canvas pieces.

**Consent agenda minutes.** The December 6, 2011 meeting opened at 7:00 p.m. under President Philippart with Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Malven, Miletti and Underwood present, Superintendent Fowler, administrators Keeling, Machesky, Rajter and Witt, and approximately 45 audience members. Resolutions 11-101 through 11-106 all passed 7-0: consent agenda; execution of the MESSA Employer Participation Agreement; and a policyholder resolution under Section 22f(1) of the State School Aid Act, 2011 PA 62, MCL 388.1622f(1), noting coverage through MESSA and, as of January 1, 2012, Blue Cross Blue Shield, ADN, National Vision Administrators and Reliance Standard. Resolution 11-104 certifies at least four of five best practices for the $100 per pupil one-time grant due by June 1, 2012 under MCL 388.1622f, citing a service consolidation resolution sent to the Michigan Department of Education on September 13, 2011, annual status reports by February 1, competitive bids on non-instructional services, and a home-page link to the MI School Data Portal; Rajter said the state would make payments in January and prorate them over eleven remaining payments. Resolution 11-105 approved Ms. Philippart's attendance at the National School Boards Association Annual Federal Relations Network Conference in Washington, D.C., February 5-7, 2012. Troy High physics teacher John Morrison's club was one of 15 high school teams nationally awarded $10,000 by Lemelson-MIT InvenTeam for a mechanical-assist stair climber. On kindergarten, Dr. Fowler stated the district would see over $3 million loss in revenue from the state if it continued a half-day program, in contrast to approximately $1.6 million to implement a full-day program; Jan Keeling said seven teachers would be needed, that Schroeder and Costello have space, and that training would run three hours; Dr. Joan Lessen-Firestone of Oakland Schools presented. Dr. Machesky reported the Summer Success Academy served 49 students entering ninth grade from Baker, Boulan Park, Larson and Smith. Facilities Study Team co-chairs Greg Bryen and Waqar Hashim committed to a recommendation at the February 7th Board Meeting. Closed session under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c) ran 8:45 p.m. to 9:38 p.m., with adjournment at 9:40 p.m.; minutes signed by Secretary Paula Fleming. The December 13, 2011 workshop ran 6:00 p.m. to 8:15 p.m. on special education finance and Schools of Choice 105 and 105C projections.

**Board action and report items.** Item 6.A appoints Jasen Witt as chief spokesperson and Mark Rajter and Sara Konieczka as team members for negotiations with TESPA/MEA/NEA, whose contract covering maintenance, special education para-educator and ELL para-educator staff expires June 30, 2012. Item 6.B recommends 2011-2012 probationary contracts for Molly Brehm, 1.0 FTE Intervention Specialist at Troy Union Elementary (B.S. Central Michigan University, December 2009; Michigan provisional certificate March 2010), and Erin Hill, 1.0 FTE Intervention Specialist at Baker Middle School (B.S. Oakland University May 2003, M.A. August 2010; Michigan professional certificate December 2011; previously Great Oaks Charter Academy). Item 7.A is Dr. Richard Machesky's report on the Oakland Community Accelerated Learning Program hosted by Oakland Community College with partner districts Avondale, Bloomfield Hills, Rochester, Pontiac and Troy, offering TSC for 2 credits, English 1510 for 3 credits, Eng 1450 for 3 credits and PSC 1560 for 4 credits (7 college credits possible), and NNO 1000 Intro to Nanotechnology for 3 credits (6 college credits possible); Troy participation is listed as Class of 2014 (18), Class of 2013 (4), English (9) and Science (45). Item 7.B presents the T.R.O.Y. (Teachers Recognizing Outstanding Youth) elementary fitness program by physical education teacher Jamie Grant, replacing the Presidential Physical Fitness Award; it spans kindergarten through fifth grade with 5 tests in grades 2 through 5, 2 tests in K and first grade, testing twice a year, and 4 awards. Items 7.C through 7.F adopt Schools of Choice resolutions under Sections 105 and 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996 for 2012-2013, advertising for 100 kindergarten and 30 first grade nonresident students and 25 nonresident sixth through eighth grade students at Baker Middle School. Item 10.A is Dr. Fowler's second of four updates on the 2011-2012 Superintendent's Goals, the next due in March, listing completion of the Facilities Study with a recommendation to the Board on February 7, 2012, a cost analysis of the data processing department, college and career readiness strategies, and expanded communication channels; the timeline notes the new district website launched in December 2011. Item 11.A is a closed session on negotiations and attorney-client privilege under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), with roll call listed for Miletti, Philippart, Schmidt, Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming and Hauff.
